regions.merged_text: God bless you and yours. I hope this finds you well and that your dear Mother's health has improved since your short visit here to Saint Felix. Thanks be to God we are all well notwithstand- ing our prevalence of real "grip weather. Dear Monsignor Hickey: you will hardly be surprised if I tell your Right Reverence that for quite some time I've been want- ing to write you; and this concerning two problems, some details of which I am sure will be a relief to your Rt. Reverence - as the release, I feel will be to me. For whether a matter be trifling or tremdous the wisdom of Jesus' dictum must always hold: "Know the Truth and the Truth will make you free." The first problem concerns the origin of the Mercy Hall Cancer Hospital of Detroit. I probably should have given you the details long ago that I now finally propose to release - details - which few, if any other could offer, details which, together with the here inclosed letter, (as a sample), will change your view of said institution and with the grace of God, I trust may completely reverse the hitherto shown attitude toward the foundress by your Rt. Rev. Paternity. Ah! for your own joyous relief as well as her estremely tried fortitude. I beg pardon for such culpable hesita- tion. Glory be to God. Following are a few details. About twenty-five years back two young nurses came to Saint Bonaventure Monastery in Detroit seeking guidance in regard to starting a cancer-hospital. I enrolled them in the Seraphic Mass Association and promised to pray for them and their project. This repeated itself a number of times for two or more years; so that I was inclined to take them for a "sort of dreamers" (?) .
